Assetauth/AdminVault.sol
StatusResolved: See Resolution
RatingSeverity: High Impact: Medium Likelihood: High
<|det|>title [68, 255, 178, 273]<|/det|>Description <|det|>text [66, 295, 930, 325]<|/det|>Fee timestamps are crucial for calculating the payments users owe to Brava during interactions, however, users can directly manipulate these timestamps, potentially avoiding any fee payments. <|det|>text [67, 337, 930, 370]<|/det|>A user can interact directly with the AdminVault contract through their Safe wallet by sending a transaction to the setFeeTimestamp() function, specifying the pool addresses where they hold active deposits. <|det|>text [66, 385, 931, 452]<|/det|>There are no access restrictions on this function, allowing the user to update the lastFeeTimestamp for both their Safe wallet and the specified pool to the current timestamp. Because lastFeeTimestamp plays a critical role in the _calculateFee() function, which assesses fees for nearly all user actions, this could enable a user to maliciously update the timestamp before withdrawing funds, thereby evading fee payments. <|det|>title [68, 484, 238, 500]<|/det|>Recommendations <|det|>text [67, 523, 588, 538]<|/det|>Users should not have unrestricted access to alter their fee timestamp. <|det|>text [67, 551, 816, 567]<|/det|>Addressing this vulnerability would likely require significant modifications to the fee protocol's design. <|det|>title [68, 600, 169, 615]<|/det|>Resolution <|det|>text [66, 638, 931, 682]<|/det|>Brava Labs have added a guard to the Safe wallets that end users deploy. This restricts calls made from the Safe wallet to only be sent to the SequenceExecutor contract which, in turn, checks that only approved actions are performed from the Safe wallet. <|det|>footer [75, 925, 206, 945]<|/det|>sigmaprime <|det|>page_number [820, 931, 883, 946]<|/det|>Page | 8

BRAV-04Disabling Fee Module From The Safe Wallet Prevents Fee Collection
Assetauth/FeeTakeSafeModule.sol
StatusResolved: See Resolution
RatingSeverity: HighImpact: MediumLikelihood: High
<|det|>title [68, 255, 178, 273]<|/det|>Description <|det|>text [66, 295, 931, 325]<|/det|>Safe wallet owners can disable the fee-taking module from their wallets by utilising the built-in module management functionality. Consequently, bots will be unable to collect fees from these wallets. <|det|>text [66, 338, 931, 381]<|/det|>The fee collection mechanism relies on whitelisted bots invoking the FeeTakeSafeModule.takeFees() function to extract fees from Safe wallets. This function initiates a zero-amount deposit which is executed in the context of the Safe wallet using the function execTransactionFromModule(): <|det|>text [73, 391, 451, 460]<|/det|>bool success = IsSafe(_safeAddr).execTransactionFromModule( SEQUENCE_EXECUTOR_ADDR, msg.value, sequencdata, enum.Departition_DelegateCall ); <|det|>text [66, 469, 931, 513]<|/det|>Malicious Safe wallet owners can bypass this mechanism by simply disabling the fee-taking module from their wallet using disableModule() function. This action effectively prevents bots from executing the takeFees() function and collecting the intended fees. <|det|>title [68, 546, 238, 561]<|/det|>Recommendations <|det|>text [67, 585, 892, 600]<|/det|>Safe wallet users should not be able to disable the fee module from their wallet to prevent regular fee collection. <|det|>text [67, 613, 884, 629]<|/det|>Addressing this vulnerability would likely require significant modifications to the design of the Safe fee module. <|det|>text [66, 641, 931, 672]<|/det|>Note, the users who disable the fee module would still end up paying fees to Brava, but only when they interact with the protocol through new deposits or withdrawals. <|det|>title [68, 704, 169, 719]<|/det|>Resolution <|det|>text [66, 743, 931, 787]<|/det|>Brava Labs have added a guard to the Safe wallets that end users deploy. This restricts calls made from the Safe wallet to only be sent to the SequenceExecutor contract which, in turn, checks that only approved actions are performed from the Safe wallet. <|det|>footer [73, 925, 206, 945]<|/det|>sigm deadline <|det|>page_number [810, 931, 884, 946]<|/det|>Page | 10

StatusResolved: See Resolution
RatingSeverity: Medium Impact: Medium Likelihood: Medium
<|det|>title [68, 254, 178, 272]<|/det|>Description <|det|>text [66, 293, 931, 323]<|/det|>Users are intended to pay an annual fee based on deposit size to Brava, this annual fee can be bypassed via various means which remove the liquidity provider tokens from the protocol. <|det|>text [88, 345, 930, 388]<|/det|>1. Some pool withdraw action contracts include a function called exit(). This function was intended as an escape hatch should a code error cause a DoS situation to occur with fee payments. However, as this function has no access control, it can be used at any time to exit the system without paying accrued interest to Brava. <|det|>text [87, 396, 931, 439]<|/det|>2. Likewise, the SendToken s action can be used to remove the tokenised representations of liquidity such as a Tokens used by Aave. Once removed, these positions can then be exited using the frontend of the underlying protocol, again, avoiding payment of fees to Brava. <|det|>text [87, 447, 931, 490]<|/det|>3. More advanced users would also be able to design their own calls that make use of the Safe wallet's existing ability to call() or delegatecall() other contracts to achieve the same result of removing supplied assets without paying any fees to Brava. <|det|>title [68, 523, 240, 539]<|/det|>Recommendations <|det|>text [66, 562, 931, 593]<|/det|>Completely preventing this issue is likely to be impossible due to the flexibility afforded by a Safe wallet to the end user. However, for Brava's intended target audience the following steps may help enforce intended action flows: <|det|>text [91, 614, 930, 645]<|/det|>- Restrict the SendToken action from sending known liquidity tokens supported by the pools. A list of these tokens could be stored in AdminVault which could then be checked against on transfers. <|det|>text [91, 654, 930, 684]<|/det|>- Remove the exit() function or add an emergency exit state that must be triggered globally prior to it being available to users. <|det|>title [68, 716, 172, 731]<|/det|>Resolution <|det|>text [67, 755, 578, 770]<|/det|>Multiple steps have been taken by the Brava team to solve this issue: <|det|>text [91, 792, 755, 808]<|/det|>- Action contracts with the exit() function have had it removed as it was a stale design. <|det|>text [91, 817, 930, 851]<|/det|>- When calling the SendToken action it is checked that the feeTimestamp has been updated at the same time. If not then the call to SendToken will revert, prompting the user to pay the owed fees. <|det|>text [91, 858, 931, 901]<|/det|>- Brava Labs have added a guard to the Safe wallets that end users deploy. This restricts calls made from the Safe wallet to only be sent to the SequenceExecutor contract which, in turn, checks that only approved actions are performed from the Safe wallet. <|det|>footer [73, 925, 206, 945]<|/det|>unespprime <|det|>page_number [810, 931, 881, 946]<|/det|>Page | 11
